author: Chicago City Wire
title: Ozgur Dede appointed chief of staff at Shriners Children's Southern California
text:
Ozgur Dede, M.D., has been named the new chief of staff at Shriners Children’s Southern California, effective January 2, 2026. Dr. Dede previously held the role of associate medical director at Shriners Children’s Erie from 2016 to 2021 and became chief of staff there in 2023.
“I am looking forward to continuing my tenure with Shriners Children’s and to serving our children and their families in Southern California,” said Dr. Dede. Chief Medical Officer Fran Farley, M.D., commented on the appointment: “Dr. Dede is a seasoned leader who has already shown a long commitment to the Shriners Children’s mission. I’m confident our patients and staff at Shriners Children’s Southern California will continue to thrive and grow under Dr. Dede’s leadership.”
Dr. Dede received his medical degree in 2001 from Hacettepe University School of Medicine in Ankara, Turkey, where he also completed an orthopedic surgery residency. He continued his training in the United States with fellowships at several institutions, including spine surgery at the University of California, San Francisco; pediatric orthopedic surgery at Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh of UPMC; pediatric orthopedic surgery at Nemours/Alfred I. duPont Hospital for Children in Wilmington, Delaware; and adult and pediatric spine surgery at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital.
After his training, Dr. Dede joined UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh in 2014 and was promoted to associate professor in 2019. He has served as division chief of pediatric orthopedic surgery since 2024.
His areas of expertise include general pediatric orthopedics, neuromuscular disease, spine deformity, and foot and hip deformity in newborns and children. Dr. Dede is a member of several professional organizations such as the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons, Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America, and Scoliosis Research Society.
Dr. Dede is also active in research and education, having published work on topics including fractures and spinal deformity as well as contributing chapters on scoliosis and skeletal injury for various books. He has been involved in teaching medical students, training residents and fellows, mentoring young professionals, reviewing for the Journal of Pediatric Orthopaedics, and serving as an associate editor for Acta Orthopedica Traumatologica Turcica.
